svg.title: The oscillator benchmark's ground truth and what it rewards
svg.desc: Left: position q1 over 3.75 seconds for the n = 8 coupled oscillators. The noise-free ODE solution from the prior mean (green dashed) passes through the values read off the paper's Figure 3 (red dots); six genuine sample paths with the stated noise level (grey) wander far from it. Right: RMSE of an extended Kalman filter as its trust in the measurements is lowered, on log-log axes. With the noise-free truth (blue) the error falls monotonically, crossing the paper's SKF value 0.0103 at trust 0.03; with a truth drawn from the model (orange) the error is about 0.23 and smallest at trust 1, the correctly tuned filter.
svg.text: The coupled-oscillator benchmark rewards a filter for ignoring its data
q₁(t), n = 8: what Fig. 3 calls ground truth
vs. genuine σ = 0.4 paths from the same start
noise-free ODE from the prior mean
EKF error vs. trust in the measurements, n = 4
Left: real paths drift 0.3–1 away from the ODE, while the plotted truth stays on it.
Right: with that truth the error falls the less the filter listens; at trust 0.03 it equals the SKF's reported 0.0103.
